correctness.rationale: The lower bound 2^(1/p) follows by unit witnesses on coordinates where the base vector has arbitrarily small fiber norm. For q>=2, the rotated fiber vector (s,-r) has the same ell_q norm as (r,s), and scalar Clarkson gives both symmetric fiber chords at least 2^(1/q); scaling this witness coordinatewise gives the global lower bound 2^(1/q). For the one-coordinate base point, one sign makes the first fiber coordinate contract, yielding min-fiber^q<=1+a^q. The outer remainder has p-mass 1-a^p, so the problem is exactly H(a)=(1+a^q)^(p/q)+1-a^p. For p<=q, subadditivity gives H<=2; for p>=q, H is increasing in a^q and H<=2^(p/q). The q=infinity endpoint is direct.
risks: The lower fresh-coordinate argument uses only a supremum when the outer support is all of a countably infinite index set; coordinates tending to zero suffice.
The checker samples parameters and is not the proof of the continuum theorem.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a closed phase law for a two-parameter classical family of vector-valued sequence spaces and identifies which geometry controls the worst local symmetric chord. The transition moves with the intrinsic fiber exponent q rather than remaining at the Hilbert value 2. The proof isolates two sharp mechanisms—almost-disjoint outer support and a rotated Clarkson fiber witness—and shows exactly where each dominates.
risks: The theorem is deliberately restricted to two-dimensional super-Hilbert fibers; the sub-Hilbert and higher-dimensional cases may have different behavior.
